Subject: Elevated availability & latency language for our order form

Vanessa —

Thanks for the quick demo last week. CardioHealth is preparing for a pilot with a patient-facing feature and procurement has asked us to capture explicit uptime and latency commitments in the order form tied to our Dedicated deployment. High level asks:

- Availability: 99.95% monthly (measurement across our primary region)
- Latency: P95 inference latency <= 350ms for typical 256-token prompts
- Credit model: pro-rated monthly credits for breaches (we've proposed 10% monthly bill for single-month breach; scaling for repeat breaches)

We also need evidence requirements: monthly uptime report, access to per-route latency histograms and a 30-day audit log export on request. We understand that some maintenance windows are required — can you propose carveouts?

I've attached a spreadsheet with our proposed language and examples (CardioHealth-SLA-requests.xlsx). Can you confirm whether Redwood can commit to this in the order form or whether we should go to an SLA addendum?

Happy to hop on a call if it's easier.

Subject: Re: CardioHealth SLA asks — reliability input

Vanessa / Aditya —

Reviewed CardioHealth's spreadsheet. From a reliability and measurement perspective here are our recommended guardrails (to include in the annotated order form/exhibit):

1) Scope: Custom availability commitment applies to Dedicated clusters that are capacity-reserved and pinned to the customer's model version. We cannot offer that availability for best-effort shared-hosting variants.

2) Measurement window & definition: Monthly availability measured as (total seconds of service uptime / total seconds in calendar month) for the customer's primary region. Downtime is defined as sustained 5+ minute per-route unavailability as observed by Redwood's synthetic probes AND a matching internal error-rate spike. This avoids noisy transient spikes being treated as downtime.

3) Scheduled maintenance: Allow up to 6 hours/month scheduled maintenance for major runtime upgrades (we will notify 7 days in advance). Scheduled windows are excluded from availability calculation. Emergency maintenance (security patches) will be coordinated and may be subject to credit rules per the exhibit.

4) Latency: P95 latency measured across the customer's production routes with 'standard' request size (we should define the 256-token benchmark in the exhibit). Provide a 30-day rolling latency histogram via Redwood Console and monthly export on request.

5) Credits: Recommend a capped credit model tied to the Dedicated monthly recurring charge only (not professional services or third-party infra). Example: single-month breach = 10% of Dedicated monthly fee, second breach within 6 months = 20%, third breach triggers review but not automatic termination.

6) Pilot & evidence: Propose a 6-month pilot where credits are capped and measurement tooling is validated. During pilot, we provide weekly availability reports and one 30-day audit log export. After pilot, we can reassess SLA levels.

7) Fallbacks: Include automatic fallback to a compatible model variant or region if capacity constraints cause elevated latency; we will document acceptable alternative model variants in the exhibit.

If Legal wants stricter wording, we should keep the exhibit explicit about definitions and measurement method. Attaching a short spec with measurement endpoints and reporting cadence.

Grace
Grace O'Connor
Head of Reliability, Redwood Inference

Subject: Fwd: CardioHealth SLA asks — proposed order form language and next steps

Mike —

Looping you back in with our internal recommendation and a proposal for concrete order-form wording. Below are the discrete items we suggest adding as a custom SLA exhibit to the Order Form. If CardioHealth is comfortable with these, we'll prepare redlines for Legal and route a DocuSign schedule.

Proposed exhibit bullets (draft):
- Applicability: This Exhibit applies only to Dedicated capacity reserved by CardioHealth in the named region for the term described in the Order Form.
- Availability target: 99.95% monthly availability measured per the Measurement Spec (see attachment). Scheduled maintenance (<= 6 hours/month with >= 7 days notice) excluded.
- Latency target: P95 inference latency <= 350ms for requests consistent with the 256-token benchmark; Redwood will publish the specific test harness and sample payload in the Measurement Spec.
- Credits: For a single monthly breach, CardioHealth is eligible for a credit equal to 10% of the Dedicated monthly fee; subsequent breaches within a rolling 6-month window will increase the credit band to 20%. Credits applied only to Dedicated recurring fees.
- Evidence: Redwood will provide monthly availability reports via the Redwood Console and will supply one 30-day audit log export per 6-month period on request; additional exports subject to reasonable fees.
- Pilot: Initial 6-month pilot with capped credits (max 10% in pilot months) to validate measurement and tooling; exhibit becomes fully effective after successful pilot or mutual agreement.

Next steps: please confirm three items so we can proceed with redlines — (1) primary region vs. multi-region measurement scope, (2) acceptance of a 6-month pilot, (3) whether credits should apply to the entire invoice or only Dedicated recurring fees. Once confirmed we'll produce the order-form redlines and share with your contracts team.

I'll attach the annotated draft and the measurement spec for your review. If it's easier, let's do a 30-minute call tomorrow morning to finalize details.

Best,
Vanessa Ortiz
Enterprise Account Executive, Redwood Inference
